1. Record Q3 revenues of nearly $151 million exceeded the high end of guidance by more than $9 million.
2. Texas (Fab 25) contributed nearly $87 million of wafer services revenue in Q3, which was $9 million above the midpoint of expectations.
3. Adjusted EBITDA of $25.8 million significantly exceeded the expected range of $10 million to $12 million for Q3.
4. SkyWater signed 4 new Quantum customer engagements since Q2, bringing total active commercial Quantum customers to 7.
5. SkyWater expects to exceed 30% revenue growth with Quantum customers in fiscal 2025 and anticipates similar growth in 2026.
6. Q4 revenue guidance is $155 million to $165 million, expected to be a new record.
7. Management expressed strong confidence that initial 2026 baseline expectations of at least $600 million revenue and at least $60 million adjusted EBITDA will prove conservative.
8. Total debt outstanding at quarter end was $184 million, an increase of $118 million from Q2 due to Fab 25 acquisition financing.
9. Gross margin guidance for 2026 improved to mid- to upper teens from mid-teens previously, representing roughly 200 basis points of improvement.
10. A potential $5 million net loss on tools may be recorded in Q4 if SkyWater is unsuccessful in securing additional funding to cover inflation-related cost increases for Florida facility tooling.

1. U.S. same-restaurant sales declined 4.7% in Q3, driven by a decrease in traffic partially offset by higher average check.
2. U.S. company-operated restaurants outperformed the broader U.S. system by 400 basis points in same-restaurant sales, declining only 0.7%.
3. International system-wide sales grew 8.6% with 3% same-restaurant sales growth, and international net unit growth is expected to exceed 9% in 2025.
4. U.S. digital sales increased 14.9% year-over-year, bringing U.S. digital mix to an all-time high of 20.3%.
5. The company increased its free cash flow outlook by $35 million to $195 million to $210 million, driven by reduced capital expenditures and tax benefits.
6. Management estimates approximately a mid-single-digit percentage of U.S. restaurants could close as part of the system optimization initiative.
7. Capital expenditures and build-to-suit investments outlook was reduced by $30 million at the midpoint to $135 million to $145 million, reflecting a shift from U.S. net unit growth to AUV growth priorities.
8. Commodity inflation outlook for the year increased to approximately 5%, up from 4%, primarily driven by continued beef price inflation.
9. The company returned over $300 million to shareholders year-to-date through dividends and share repurchases, and remains on track to exceed $325 million for the full year.
10. Adjusted EBITDA rose 2.1% to $138 million in Q3, while adjusted EPS was $0.24 per share versus $0.25 in the prior year.

1. KKR reported fee related earnings of $1.15 per share, total operating earnings of $1.55 per share, and adjusted net income of $1.41 per share in Q3 2025, all among the highest figures in the company's history as a public company.
2. Management fees were $1.1 billion in Q3, up 19% year-over-year (16% excluding catch-up fees of over $40 million).
3. KKR raised $43 billion of capital in Q3 2025, making it the second highest fundraising quarter in company history, with credit platform inflows comprising roughly 60% of the total.
4. The K-Series private wealth products brought in $4.1 billion in Q3, up 20% from the prior quarter and 80% above the year-ago figure, with total K-Series AUM now exceeding $32 billion compared to $15 billion a year ago.
5. KKR has approximately $17 billion of embedded gains across the firm (gross unrealized carry and unrealized investment gains), the second highest level in its history, up 10% from a year ago and over 50% from two years ago.
6. The company expects a Q4 charge of approximately $350 million related to a clawback from the underperforming Asia II private equity fund, which will reduce Q4 ANI per share by about $0.18.
7. Year-to-date realized carry is up over 50%, while the unrealized carry balance has grown 14% year-to-date despite active monetizations.
8. KKR's credit platform raised $55 billion year-to-date, already approaching the $56 billion raised over all of 2024, positioning 2025 to be a record credit fundraising year.
9. Total insurance-related economics were approximately $1.4 billion year-to-date (net of compensation), up 16% compared to the same period last year.
10. Management reaffirmed confidence in 2026 guidance of $4.50+ in FRE per share and $7+ in after-tax ANI per share, noting the company has over $800 million to $1 billion of monetization visibility over the next two quarters.

1. Q3 adjusted operating EBITDA was $519 million, a 7% year-over-year increase, with margin improving 130 basis points to 19.3%.
2. Q3 revenue was nearly $2.7 billion, flat against a strong 9% comparable from the prior year.
3. The company reached approximately 2.5x net debt to EBITDA and reduced gross debt by more than $3 billion year-over-year.
4. Food Ingredients delivered adjusted operating EBITDA margin improvement of 230 basis points in Q3 and over 400 basis points over the past 2 years, on track to achieve mid-teen EBITDA margin.
5. Scent segment delivered 5% sales growth with Fine Fragrance up 20% year-over-year.
6. Full year 2025 guidance was reiterated with sales expected at $10.6 billion to $10.9 billion and adjusted operating EBITDA between $2.0 billion and $2.15 billion.
7. The $500 million share repurchase program commenced October 1, targeting at minimum $80 million annually to offset dilution.
8. Free cash flow for 2025 is expected to be modestly below the $500 million target due to higher inventories and portfolio-related costs.
9. The pending divestiture of the Soy Crush, Concentrates & Lecithin business to Bunge is expected to generate approximately $90 million in net cash proceeds.
10. The Health North America and Fragrance Ingredients businesses combined represent about 5% of total company sales and are expected to see trend improvements in 2026.

1. Fiscal 2025 was Applied Materials' sixth consecutive year of growth, with revenue and earnings growing at annualized rates of approximately 12% and 20%, respectively.
2. Revenue grew 4% to $28.4 billion in fiscal 2025, with non-GAAP gross margin increasing 120 basis points to 48.8%, the highest level in 25 years.
3. China declined to 28% of total systems and service revenues in fiscal 2025 and to 25% for the fourth quarter, with the company expecting lower wafer fab equipment spending in China in 2026.
4. The impact of trade restrictions on Applied's accessible China market more than doubled from around 10% in fiscal 2024 to over 20% in fiscal 2025.
5. DRAM revenues from leading-edge customers grew by more than 50% over the past four fiscal quarters.
6. Applied Global Services revenue grew 3% to a record $6.4 billion, with the recurring parts, services and software portion growing by double digits.
7. The company distributed approximately $6.3 billion to shareholders, including $1.4 billion in dividends and $4.9 billion in share repurchases, reducing shares outstanding by more than 3%.
8. Q1 fiscal 2026 guidance includes revenue of $6.85 billion (±$500 million) and non-GAAP EPS of $2.18 (±$0.20), with non-GAAP gross margin expected at approximately 48.4%.
9. The company estimates approximately $600 million in trade restriction-related revenue will be spread through the rest of fiscal 2026 following the reinstatement of suspended affiliate rules.
10. The advanced packaging business is currently around $1.5 billion and the company expects to double it to $3 billion or more over the next few years.

1. Fiscal year 2025 revenue was $8.13 billion, representing 7.4% year-over-year growth.
2. Non-GAAP EPS for fiscal 2025 was $6.04, a 14.4% increase year-over-year.
3. Cash flow from operations for fiscal 2025 was $621 million, achieved while driving 7% revenue growth.
4. The ZT Systems acquisition closed with an estimated purchase price of $2.05 billion, including up to $450 million in contingent consideration based on 3-year financial performance.
5. ZT Systems has an annual revenue run rate of approximately $5 billion to $6 billion, with Q1 FY2026 contribution expected at $850 million to $1.05 billion for 2 months post-closing.
6. Q1 FY2026 guidance includes total revenue of $2.9 billion to $3.2 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.95 to $2.25, representing 52% and 46.3% year-over-year growth at midpoints respectively.
7. Management now expects to reach $16 billion in revenue within 2 years, accelerated from the prior 3-year target.
8. Non-GAAP pretax ROIC improved to 28.3% in Q4 from 23.0% in the same period a year ago.
9. The company secured $2.0 billion Term Loan A and $800 million Term Loan B for the acquisition, with $2.2 billion of funded debt at closing and revolver capacity increased to $1.5 billion.
10. Long-term non-GAAP operating margin target is 6% to 7% or higher, compared to the short-term guidance range of 5.6% to 6.1%.

1. Q3 2025 revenue was $29.1 million, up 32% year-over-year, with Software Products & Services growing 55% year-over-year.
2. Excluding Veritone Hire, Software Products & Services revenue surged by more than 200% year-over-year.
3. The company agreed to retire 100% of its senior secured term debt and repurchase 50% of its convertible notes for approximately $77.5 million in cash and 625,000 shares.
4. Annual debt service burden dropped from over $14 million to approximately $800,000 following the debt paydown.
5. Veritone Data Refinery (VDR) qualified pipeline and bookings now exceed $40 million, reflecting 100% growth quarter-over-quarter.
6. Non-GAAP net loss from continuing operations improved 48% year-over-year to $5.8 million in Q3 2025.
7. Public Sector pipeline now approaches $218 million in qualified opportunities, up from $110 million earlier in 2025.
8. Q4 2025 revenue guidance is $33.4 million to $39.4 million, representing a 63% increase at the midpoint year-over-year.
9. The company expects to achieve operating profitability in late 2026 and has approximately $34 million in unencumbered cash post-debt paydown to fund operations through that period.
10. ARR reached $68.8 million, up 9% year-over-year, with consumption-based customer ARR increasing 26% year-over-year and 74% sequentially.

1. Americold delivered Q4 2025 AFFO of $0.38 per share, slightly ahead of expectations, and full year 2025 AFFO of $1.43 per share.
2. The company is guiding full year 2026 AFFO between $1.20 and $1.30 per share, representing a year-over-year decline from $1.43.
3. Leverage stood at 6.8x net debt to pro forma core EBITDA at the end of Q4, and management is targeting a meaningful reduction to 6x or below to maintain investment-grade status.
4. Americold expects 2026 same-store revenue of approximately $2.2 billion to $2.27 billion and same-store NOI of $735 million to $785 million.
5. The company expects 2026 revenue per pallet to decline 100 to 200 basis points and economic occupancy to be flat to down 300 basis points due to customers tightening space commitments at contract renewal.
6. Americold has identified $30 million in annualized cost savings from indirect warehouse labor and SG&A, with actions largely completed, and expects to reduce Project Orion cash spend by approximately $50 million in 2026.
7. During 2025, the company strategically exited or idled 10 sites in North America, removing over 22 million cubic feet of capacity (65,000+ pallet positions), and has identified 9 additional sites for action in 2026.
8. Approximately 60% of rent and storage revenues now come from fixed commitment contracts, up from less than 40% a few years ago, with high retention rates on renewals though customers are tightening the gap between physical and economic occupancy.
9. The deleveraging initiative through potential JV or asset sales is seeing strong interest from multiple investors at attractive valuations, but no unannounced transactions are included in the 2026 AFFO guidance.
10. The U.S. cold storage market has seen in excess of 15% incremental capacity added in recent years primarily by new market entrants, though new development announcements have slowed materially and the company believes peak deliveries have passed.

1. Q3 revenue was $886 million, an increase of 28% year-over-year and above the high end of guidance.
2. Sequential usage growth from non-AI existing customers in Q3 was the highest in 12 quarters.
3. New logo annualized bookings more than doubled year-over-year and set a new record, driven by an increase in average new logo land size, particularly in enterprise.
4. AI native customers represented 12% of revenue in Q3, up from 11% last quarter and approximately 6% in the year-ago quarter.
5. Revenue growth excluding the AI native customer group was 20% year-over-year in Q3, accelerating from 18% year-over-year in Q2.
6. Security ARR growth was in the mid-50s percentage year-over-year in Q3, up from the mid-40s mentioned last quarter.
7. Digital experience products together exceed $300 million in ARR, with Product Analytics already adopted by more than 1,000 customers.
8. RPO was $2.79 billion, up 53% year-over-year, with current RPO growth in the low 50s percentage year-over-year.
9. The company now has more than 500 AI native customers, with about 100 spending more than $100,000 annually and more than 15 spending more than $1 million annually.
10. Q4 2025 revenue guidance is $912 million to $916 million, representing 24% year-over-year growth, with full-year 2025 revenue expected to be $3.386 billion to $3.390 billion, representing 26% year-over-year growth.

1. Full year fiscal 2025 revenue reached a record $21.8 billion with 7.7% reported growth and 2.9% organic growth, while adjusted diluted EPS reached a record $14.40, representing 9.6% growth including a 2-point tariff impact.
2. The company returned $2.2 billion to shareholders in fiscal 2025, including a $1 billion share buyback, and announced its 54th consecutive year of dividend increases.
3. Adjusted gross margin increased 140 basis points and adjusted operating margin expanded 80 basis points to reach a record 25% for fiscal 2025.
4. Fiscal 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance is set at $14.75 to $15.05, with Q1 EPS expected in the range of $2.75 to $2.85.
5. The company expects $185 million or 80 basis points in incremental year-over-year tariff headwinds in fiscal 2026.
6. Alaris pump installations reached record levels in fiscal 2025, but will create a headwind to fiscal 2026 growth of over 100 basis points as remediation completes.
7. China is expected to decline mid-teens in fiscal 2026, impacting overall growth by approximately 100 basis points, with volume-based procurement expected to reach 80% portfolio coverage by year-end.
8. Pharm Systems vaccines, approximately 20% of segment revenue, are expected to decline approximately 25% in fiscal 2026, creating a 50 basis point impact to overall growth.
9. The company initiated a 2-year $200 million cost-out program with approximately half expected in fiscal 2026, while investing an incremental $30 million in sales force expansion for high-growth markets.
10. BD plans to execute a $250 million share buyback this quarter and will use at least half of the $4 billion cash proceeds from the Waters transaction for share repurchases following the expected close around end of Q1 calendar 2026.

1. Full year 2025 revenue increased 12.5% to approximately $990 million, and adjusted EBITDA improved 5.7% to $582 million.
2. Ormat secured approximately 200 megawatts of new PPAs with hyperscalers and data centers, including a 15-year portfolio PPA for up to 150 megawatts with Google through NV Energy and a 20-year PPA with Switch for approximately 13 megawatts.
3. Two negotiated blend-and-extend contracts totaling approximately 40 megawatts are pending final approval and are expected to improve revenues at two facilities by approximately $20 to $30 per megawatt hour beginning in 2027.
4. For 2026, the company expects revenue to range between $1,110 million and $1,160 million (14.6% increase at midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA between $615 million and $645 million (8.2% increase at midpoint).
5. Energy Storage segment revenue grew 109.3% to $79 million for the full year and reported gross margins of 51.5% in Q4 and 36.4% for the full year, a significant improvement versus the prior year.
6. Curtailments in the U.S. Electricity segment reduced revenues by $18.6 million in 2025, but management expects only $4 million to $6 million in curtailment impact in 2026.
7. The company collected more than $180 million in cash monetization of PTCs and ITCs in 2025, exceeding the anticipated $160 million, and expects to collect approximately $90 million from ITC transactions and transfers in 2026.
8. Total capital expenditure for 2026 is expected to be $675 million, with a net investment of approximately $575 million after the ~$100 million Topp 2 plant sale in New Zealand, and the company has total available liquidity of $680 million.
9. The company has safe-harbored over 1 gigawatt of energy storage projects and currently has 6 storage projects under development expected to add 410 megawatts or 1,540 megawatt hours to its portfolio.
10. Management plans to hold an Analyst Day in September 2026 to provide longer-term megawatt growth targets, and is currently developing 182 megawatts of geothermal capacity in Indonesia across multiple concessions.

1. Q3 U.S. comparable restaurant sales were up 120 basis points with traffic down only 10 basis points, representing a 130 basis point and 190 basis point improvement respectively versus Q2.
2. The company is raising full year 2025 adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $1.10 to $1.15, up from prior guidance, with Q4 EPS expected between $0.23 and $0.28.
3. Bloomin' Brands identified approximately $75 million of turnaround investments across 2026-2028, with approximately $50 million in 2026, to be offset by approximately $80 million in non-guest-facing productivity savings over the same period.
4. The company closed 21 underperforming restaurants last week and identified 22 additional restaurants where it will not renew leases, with most expiring in the next 4 years.
5. The dividend has been suspended, with available free cash flow to be used for debt paydown targeting lease-adjusted leverage of 3.0x by the end of 2028.
6. Outback achieved its first quarter of positive comp sales (up 40 basis points with flat traffic) since Q2 2023, with steak test enhancements delivering an average 10-point lift across guest satisfaction, taste, value, and intent to reorder.
7. Q3 adjusted operating margins declined 150 basis points year-over-year to 0.8%, driven by COGS inflation of 4.9%, labor inflation of 3.3%, and 60 basis points of higher insurance expense.
8. The company expects to receive approximately $122 million from the second Brazil refranchising installment this month, which will reduce lease-adjusted net leverage from 4.3x to 4.0x on a pro forma basis.
9. Carrabba's delivered the strongest brand performance with comp sales up 410 basis points and positive traffic of 60 basis points in Q3.
10. The company plans to refresh nearly 100% of Outback restaurants by the end of 2028 at an average cost of approximately $400,000 per unit, shifting capital from new restaurant builds to asset refreshes.

1. Full year 2025 revenue was approximately $2.433 billion, a 20.2% increase over the prior year, and full year adjusted EBITDA was $320.8 million, a 74.8% increase over the prior year.
2. Q4 2025 revenue was approximately $662 million, up 27.4% year-over-year, and Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $85 million, up 54% year-over-year, with results benefiting from a 53rd accounting week.
3. The company provided 2026 guidance of revenue between $2.54 billion and $2.56 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $318 million to $322 million, excluding the impact of the Family First acquisition.
4. The Family First Homecare acquisition is valued at $175.5 million (approximately 7.5x post-synergy EBITDA), with roughly $120 million in annual revenue (about two-thirds from Florida), and is expected to close in late Q2 2026.
5. Free cash flow for 2025 was $131 million, with total liquidity of approximately $529 million at quarter-end including $193 million cash on hand and an undrawn $226 million revolver.
6. Private Duty Services preferred payer agreements grew from 22 to 30 in 2025 with a target of 38 by end of 2026, and preferred payer volumes accounted for approximately 57% of total PDS MCO volumes in Q4, expected to reach the low 60% range in 2026.
7. Home Health & Hospice Q4 episodic payer mix reached 78% with total episodic volume growth of 25% and total admissions of 10,400 (up 22.4% year-over-year), and the company expects episodic mix to remain above 75% with organic growth approaching double digits in 2026.
8. Medical Solutions Q4 gross margin of 50% was elevated by a $2.5 million to $3 million reserve release from stronger-than-expected cash collections, and is expected to normalize to the 43% to 45% range in Q1 2026.
9. The company achieved 10 state Medicaid rate enhancements in 2025 and expects high single-digit (6 to 8) state rate enhancements in 2026, with increases being more cost-of-living oriented in the 1% to 5% range rather than the larger structural resets seen previously.
10. The company had approximately $1.49 billion in variable rate debt at Q4 end, with $520 million hedged via fixed rate swaps (through June 2026) and $880 million subject to an interest rate cap limiting SOFR exposure above 3% (through February 2027), and net leverage stood at approximately 4x.

1. Q3 2025 EsoGuard test volume was 2,841 tests with revenue of approximately $1.2 million, in line with Q2 2025 and within the target range of 2,500 to 3,000 tests per quarter.
2. Cash position at quarter end was $47.3 million following a completed public offering that netted approximately $27 million in proceeds.
3. Quarterly burn rate was $10.3 million, consisting of $7.2 million from ongoing operations and $3.1 million from the quarterly MSA with PAVmed.
4. Up to 50% of the company's 30 million target patient population are Medicare eligible, while current Medicare testing represents only about 10% to 15% of volume.
5. Once final Medicare coverage is secured, the company will be able to submit and receive payment for claims dating back 1 full year.
6. Of claims submitted in Q3, 76% have been adjudicated with 38% resulting in an allowable amount averaging approximately $1,600 per test.
7. The company billed over $7.1 million in pro forma revenue during Q3 but recognized only approximately 17% ($1.2 million) due to revenue recognition timing related to collection probability.
8. PAVmed remains the single largest common shareholder with approximately 23% ownership, and together with Board and management holds approximately 28% voting interest.
9. Shares outstanding including unvested RSAs are approximately 138 million, with potential for an additional 49.6 million common shares if all preferred shares were converted.
10. Variable cost per test remains under $200, comprising approximately $50 for EsoCheck and $120-125 for lab processing.

1. Gross revenue and portfolio income for Q4 2025 increased 179% to $2.4 million, compared to approximately $869,000 in Q4 2024.
2. Q4 2025 results include a $196.1 million noncash unrealized and realized loss related to mark-to-market accounting adjustments on SUI and digital asset loan receivable holdings.
3. The net loss for Q4 2025 was $221.8 million or $5.52 per diluted share, compared to a net loss of approximately $91,000 or $0.01 per diluted share in Q4 2024.
4. As of December 31, 2025, SUI Group held 105,086,451 SUI tokens with a net value of $147.4 million, plus a digital asset loan receivable of 2,961,550 SUI with a net value of $3.6 million.
5. As of December 31, 2025, cash and cash equivalents were $21.9 million, compared to $6 million as of December 31, 2024.
6. In Q4, the company repurchased approximately 7.8 million shares at an average price of $2.02 per share, representing approximately 8.8% of shares outstanding at time of implementation.
7. Since inception of the digital asset treasury strategy in July 2025, the company has generated approximately 1.13 million SUI in total staking rewards and lending activities, with staking yielding approximately 1.7% annualized.
8. The Bluefin institutional lending arrangement is currently yielding approximately 17% to 18% per annum, paid weekly in SUI.
9. The company minted $10 million of suiUSDe stablecoin deployed into an Ember-operated vault, currently yielding close to 10% on that stablecoin position.
10. Management's long-term target over the next 12 to 18 months is to achieve close to 10% yield on SUI holdings through a combination of institutional and DeFi ecosystem lending.

1. Net sales increased 12% year-over-year to $1.6 billion in 2025, driven by a 14% increase in shipments primarily from the Augusta mill operating for a full year.
2. Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations was $107 million in 2025, an improvement of $71 million versus the prior year.
3. The company faces an approximately $70 million pricing headwind in 2026 versus 2025, including a $50 million headwind from the Q4 RISI Folding Carton Index change the company disputes as inaccurate.
4. Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA is expected to be approximately breakeven, with $15 million to $20 million in incremental costs from severe weather disruptions at the Augusta and Cypress Bend facilities.
5. The company announced price increases of $60 per ton on cup grades and $50 per ton on all other products, affecting approximately 50% of volume not tied to the RISI Price Index.
6. 2026 revenue guidance is $1.4 billion to $1.5 billion with flat to modest shipment growth, and the guidance does not include any impact from the recently announced price increase or RISI's projected pricing recovery.
7. The company reduced its overall workforce by more than 10% in 2025, including a roughly 40% reduction in corporate SG&A headcount, bringing SG&A to 6.5% of net sales from 8.4% in 2024.
8. The company received an initial insurance settlement payment of $23 million in Q4 from its $105 million representation and warranty insurance policy related to the Augusta acquisition, with approximately $75 million of coverage remaining.
9. Engineering feasibility for a CUK conversion at Cypress Bend is complete with a cost estimate of $60 million and a 12- to 18-month execution timeline, targeting 100,000 to 150,000 tons of independent converter volume.
10. The company ended the year with more than $400 million in liquidity and $79 million remaining under its share repurchase authorization, with management expressing confidence in returning to cross-cycle EBITDA margins of 13% to 14% and more than $100 million of annual free cash flow.

1. Centrus achieved full year 2025 revenue of $448.7 million, gross profit of $117.5 million, and net income of $77.8 million.
2. In January 2026, the Department of Energy selected Centrus for a $900 million HALEU enrichment award, which could increase to just over $1 billion with $170 million of additional options.
3. Centrus ended 2025 with an unrestricted cash balance of approximately $2 billion, supported by $533.6 million in gross proceeds from two ATM programs and an oversubscribed convertible senior note issuance.
4. The company's total backlog stood at $3.8 billion as of December 31, 2025, extending to 2040, including a $2.3 billion contingent LEU sale backlog.
5. Centrus provided 2026 guidance of total company revenue of $425 million to $475 million (flat year-over-year at midpoint) and total capital deployment of $350 million to $500 million.
6. SWU revenue increased 21% year-over-year driven by a 23% increase in the volume of SWUs sold, while uranium revenue decreased 54% year-over-year to $55.6 million.
7. The first new cascade of centrifuges is expected to come online in 2029, with HALEU production planned before the end of the decade at a rate of 12 metric tons per year thereafter.
8. Near-term domestic LEU demand is set to increase by approximately 6.5 million SWUs due to Russia exiting the market and additional demand from restarts, uprates, and new pledged reactors, with LEU pricing experiencing a 24% compound annual growth rate from 2019 to 2025.
9. Management announced that the base case build-out is expected to be sufficient to reach nth-of-a-kind cost, which will be achieved well before 3 million SWUs of capacity, a key milestone for economic viability.
10. A scheduled fourth quarter shipment from Russia did not leave as expected due to a shipping issue and was pushed to Q1 2026, which would have positively impacted gross margin and net income for the year.

1. Expand Energy achieved a 15% reduction in breakevens in the Haynesville during 2025, which management described as a key driver of both lower reinvestment rates and improved inventory economics.
2. The company's hedging program generated $200 million in gains in 2025.
3. Management is targeting an incremental $0.20 per Mcf improvement in realizations across the business, which translates to approximately $500 million in EBITDA.
4. Maintenance capital to deliver 7.5 Bcf/day has declined by $225 million compared to a year ago, reflecting significant operational efficiency gains.
5. The company has allocated $75 million for the Western Haynesville program in 2026, with approximately 2.5 wells scheduled, the first of which has been drilled and is being completed with first production expected in late Q1 or early Q2.
6. Management expects the CEO search to take approximately 6 to 9 months, with interim Chairman Mike Wichterich committed to staying until the right candidate is found.
7. The company added 3.5 Bcf of gas storage capacity in Q4 2025, bringing its total storage position to approximately 5 Bcf.
8. Expand Energy's 2026 capital expenditure guidance is $2.85 billion to deliver average production of approximately 7.5 Bcf per day, with operational efficiency supporting volumes up to 7.75 Bcf per day.
9. Around 20% of 2025 Haynesville turn-in-lines exceeded 1 Bcf per 1,000 feet of lateral, and management expects that figure to rise above 30% in 2026 driven by advanced completion designs and cheaper self-sourced sand.
10. The company expects to become a full cash taxpayer closer to 2030, with cash taxes stair-stepping higher over the next several years due to benefits from the OBBB legislation.

1. The company delivered its second highest adjusted earnings and free cash flow in its history in 2025, returning approximately $160 million in capital to shareholders.
2. Dispensing and Specialty Closures segment now represents over half of the company's adjusted EBITDA and delivered record sales, adjusted EBIT, and adjusted EBITDA in 2025.
3. Metal Containers segment volumes grew 4% in 2025, led by 7% growth in pet food products, which now represents more than half of segment volume.
4. Custom Containers adjusted EBIT and EBITDA margins expanded by 150 basis points in 2025 to a record year of profitability.
5. Management provided 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $3.70 to $3.90 compared to $3.72 in 2025, with higher operating income partially offset by higher interest and tax expense.
6. Free cash flow for 2026 is estimated at approximately $450 million, with CapEx of approximately $310 million to support investments in dispensing and pet food products.
7. Q1 2026 adjusted EPS is expected to be $0.70 to $0.80 compared to $0.82 in the prior year period, with interest expense anticipated at approximately $45 million.
8. The Weener acquisition integration is complete with full run rate synergies achieved, and the company returned to within target leverage range just over a year after closing the transaction.
9. Management expects Dispensing and Specialty Closures organic volumes to grow low to mid-single digits in 2026, driven by mid-single-digit growth in dispensing products.
10. The healthcare business is approximately $200 million in revenue, and management expects it could double over the next 3 to 5 years through organic pipeline growth and potential acquisitions.

1. Q4 2025 revenue increased 4% year-over-year while operating expenses declined 1%, resulting in operating income growth of 35% and a 390 basis point expansion in operating margin to 16.9%.
2. Full year 2025 adjusted earnings per share was $6.21, an increase of 28% from the prior year, with operating income up 25% and operating margin expanding 260 basis points to 15.5%.
3. AI-driven productivity improvements generated approximately $30 million of expense reductions in 2025, with at least an additional $70 million of expense savings expected through the end of 2027.
4. The Education Technology Services segment grew revenue by more than 40% to nearly $150 million in 2025, with operating income increasing 38% to $59 million and an operating margin of 40%.
